19000024_61.boundary: Qwilfish uses Destiny Bond; Clefable's Return KOs it for 88; Destiny Bond activates and Clefable faints too. Showdown: |-singlemove| Destiny Bond, |-damage|p2a: Qwilfish|0 fnt, |faint|, |-activate|move: Destiny Bond, |faint|p1a: Clefable, |win|.
19000024_61.the_cause: the engine is RIGHT. It models Destiny Bond killing Clefable as Damage SideOne: 95, its full HP. Showdown kills Clefable too -- |faint|p1a: Clefable is right there -- but expresses a Destiny Bond faint as |-activate| plus |faint| with NO |-damage| LINE. So the observed component set is empty for p1 while the engine carries capped_lethal=-95, and the matcher counts an extra engine component with no observed counterpart.
19000024_61.this_cause_is_ALREADY_WRITTEN: it is the same mechanism reports/c96 recorded for 19000152/53, Perish Song: a faint with no damage event. C96's disposition applies verbatim -- 'a |faint| with no preceding |-damage| must reconcile against an engine capped_lethal equal to the victim's remaining HP'. Destiny Bond is a second member of that class, and C96 explicitly said it is NOT a comparison limit because both sides are fully determined from source.
19000024_61.why_it_was_filed_a_limit: the divergence class is self-attributing. Both slots carry capped_lethal, so the roll-divergent-lethality rule matched on shape without anyone checking whether a roll was actually in dispute. No roll is in dispute here: the engine's 88 and the observed 88 agree exactly, and the p1 disagreement is a missing EVENT, not a differing roll.

the_pattern.two_of_two: both rows examined so far are faint-without-a-damage-event, and both were already caused -- Destiny Bond and Perish Song. Neither has a roll in dispute: in 19000024/61 the engine's 88 and the observed 88 agree exactly, and in 19000077/47 there is no damage roll anywhere in the boundary.
the_pattern.why_the_class_collects_them: limit:roll_divergent_lethality matches on SHAPE -- a capped_lethal component whose counterpart is absent -- which is indistinguishable from a faint the observation never rendered as damage. The class name asserts a roll disagreement that neither row has. This is a self-attributing label doing work the evidence does not support, which is the thing the programme's rules were written against.
the_pattern.implication: if the remaining five are the same, the limit count drops from 8 to 1 -- leaving only limit:world_sample_drag_target, which IS registered and evidence-backed -- and clause 2's target becomes a single row. I am NOT claiming that. Five rows are unexamined: 19000089/53, 19000147/125, 19000191/63, 19000198/33, 19000199/61. Two of two is a pattern worth stating and not a result.
the_pattern.one_fix_may_close_several: C96's disposition -- a |faint| with no preceding |-damage| must reconcile against an engine capped_lethal equal to the victim's remaining HP -- would close 19000152/53, 19000024/61 and 19000077/47 together. That is three rows across three families for one change, and it is the cheapest remaining item in the queue.

implementing_c96s_disposition_is_not_a_o.where_the_rows_actually_fail: not at the exact-component comparison. capped_lethal is in _ROLL_SCALED_SOURCES, so these rows are rejected inside roll_component_events_agree -- observed carries no component for the slot and the engine carries capped_lethal. That is why the divergence class comes out roll-flavoured.
the_two_facts_the_fix_needs_and_does_not: that the OBSERVED protocol contains a |faint| for that side with NO preceding |-damage|. roll_component_events_agree receives component lists, not protocol lines.
the victim's REMAINING HP at that point, to check the engine's capped_lethal equals it rather than accepting any capped_lethal against an empty observation.
implementing_c96s_disposition_is_not_a_o.why_that_matters: without the first fact the rule degenerates into 'accept an unmatched engine capped_lethal', which would accept a genuine engine over-kill and is exactly the widening the programme forbids. Without the second it would accept a wrong magnitude. So the fix is a THREADING change -- carry the faint-without-damage signal and the pre-state HP into the comparison -- not a predicate tweak.
implementing_c96s_disposition_is_not_a_o.cost_estimate: modest but real: a new parameter through roll_component_events_agree's call sites, the signal derived where the protocol is parsed, a pin that fails when reverted, and a single-variable sweep. Larger than the movepainsplit change, smaller than the crit-tag work.
implementing_c96s_disposition_is_not_a_o.value: three rows across three families (19000152/53 Perish Song, 19000024/61 Destiny Bond, 19000077/47 Perish Song) for one change, plus it removes a class the limit label has been silently absorbing.
